subjects.displayTitle: Nearness and remoteness: the distances of the heart
subjects.introduction: How many who are near are strangers, Bahá’u’lláh exclaims, and how many strangers are near. ‘Abdu’l-Bahá tells an aunt burning with separation that a person a hundred thousand miles away who has won God’s good pleasure enjoys His nearness, and explains with the sun and the mirror: the sun never moves, and its presence or absence depends on whether the surface facing it is polished or rusted. Nearness and remoteness, then, name states of the heart. The prayers still give the ache of distance its full voice, pleading not to be kept from the shore of the ocean of nearness; yet an exile hears that his banishment was made a means of drawing him closer, and a friend forbidden to visit that this very distance is union. The journey ends in conduct: to live as a departed believer lived is called the nearest means of approach. The Qur’án’s assurance that God is near and answers whoever calls says as much. Ahead lie nearness to God itself, the life of the spirit, and the inner meanings of heaven and hell.
subjects.arc: Begin with the paradox of distant presence, explore nearness beyond physical location, listen to the prayers of separation and companionship, then follow recognition and love into service and daily conduct.

order.why: Read the distinction between the divine Essence and manifested nearness.
Open with the reversal of familiar and distant relationships.
Distinguish nearness of soul from nearness of body.
shortened: O thou enraptured handmaid of God! Nearness is verily of the soul, not of the body; and the help that is sought, and the help that cometh, is not material but of the spirit; nevertheless it is my hope that thou wilt attain to nearness in every sense. The bounties of God will verily encompass a sanctified soul even as the sun's light doth the moon and stars: be thou assured of this.

order.why: Read consolation through good-pleasure despite great physical distance.
shortened: However, it is clear and evident that true reunion is spiritual nearness attainable only by walking in the path of His good pleasure. Therefore, if a person is physically one hundred thousand miles away but blessed with Godis good pleasure that one is in truth among those who enjoy nearness to Him. Otherwise, that which looks outwardly near is in fact distant.

order.why: Explore the polished surface and sunlight analogy.
shortened: The spirit remains ever in its center of transcendence and elevation, like the sun constantly fixed in its orbit. Its absence and presence relate to the purity of the receiving place and the refinement of the body facing it. As soon as the facing surface is polished, the lights of the sun appear in it, and as soon as the surface becomes dense, its lights disappear from it. Thus we know that nearness and distance refer to purity and refinement versus rust, turbidity and density.

order.why: Consider purity and receptivity as spiritual nearness.
shortened: It is evident that the divine nearness is an unlimited nearness, be it in this world or the next one. This is a nearness which is sanctified from the comprehension of the minds. The more a man seeketh light from the Sun of Truth, the nearer he will draw. For instance, a clear body is near unto the sun, and a black stone is far from the sun. This nearness dependeth upon clearness, purity and perfection and that remoteness is due to density, dullness (or obscurity) and imperfection.

order.why: Examine the philosophical qualifications of language about the Friend’s nearness.
shortened: As for what was mentioned in the words of the ancients that "the Friend is nearer to me than myself" - this is a remote saying and strange utterance. How can the created be nearer to the Creator than the Creator's own Self?

Yet should ye remain distant -- that is, fail to reach unto that Reality -- in that very remoteness lieth nearness, which is the essence of grace itself, inasmuch as the signs of His manifestation are within you. And this is the verity: that communion is far from you, for ye cannot achieve the knowledge of Him, yet He is near unto your hearts, for He placeth the tokens of His own Reality therein, that thereby ye may attain unto nearness and Truth.

order.why: Consider a nearness beyond spatial opposites.
shortened: For besides this nearness and remoteness mentioned, there is a nearness with God that hath no likeness, opposite, or equal in the realm of limitations and physical places. Strive thou that through the favors of the King of Oneness thou mayest enter into that station, that thou mayest be wholly purified and sanctified from the tree of remoteness with all its fruits and leaves. This is a nearness that will never be transformed into remoteness and will endure through the eternity of God.

order.why: Keep the Bab’s paradox of nearness and remoteness in its own terms.
shortened: So establish thyself in that station and be assured that this rank, despite its perfect nearness is remote, and despite its perfect remoteness is near. God hath made it nearer to everything than anything else - neither darknesses can conceal it nor veils can hide it.

order.why: Read the symbolic points of nearness and turning away.
Distinguish spiritual kinship from outward relationship.
Consider turning toward God apart from lineage or physical proximity.
shortened: Know thou that between God and any soul there is no kinship. Whoso turneth unto God, belongeth unto Him, though he be from the people of the farthest West; and whoso turneth away is not of Him, though he be at His very side.

order.why: Read the counsel about approaching the Court and the reversal of near and far.
shortened: As to approaching the Most Holy Court in these days, this is outwardly not permitted. We have revealed in one of the Tablets: "How many are near whom We do not confirm in their nearness, and how many are remote and, by the Self of the Beloved, are yet nigh!" And in another Tablet: "How many who are near are yet strangers, and how many who are distant are yet near! Blessed is he who is near and drew near!"

order.why: Leave room for wisdom in the experiences of nearness and remoteness.
Keep the distinction between senses of nearness.
Hear the invitation to draw near with the heart.
Read the reported reversal between those near and far.
Retain the concise form of that reversal.
shortened: How many who were near were kept back, and how many who were remote attained!

order.why: Consider the contrast between the desert and mosque in the particular account.
shortened: The one who dwelt in the desert attained the outpourings of the All-Bountiful, while he who was in the mosque remained deprived.

order.why: Read presence in heart and spirit despite bodily absence.
Keep the reassurance to the distant traveler.
shortened: O suckling at the breast of providence! Though you have traveled and become distant from worldly sight, you are visible and near to the eye of heart and soul and vision and spirit.

order.why: Read remembrance as presence in a gathering.
Hear the instruction to understand oneself as present.
Read the reassurance and cited Sa’di verse with the source omission visible.
Connect steadfast love with presence before the Throne.
Consider the questions about sorrow and continual companionship.
shortened: Is it from the world, after thou hast seen it passing, passing away? Is it from thy remoteness from My presence, after the Tongue of the All-Merciful hath testified that thou art with Him at all times?

order.why: Read the consolation addressed to loneliness.
Keep the reported image of companionship in a desert.
Consider intimacy with God amid estrangement.
shortened: I beseech God that at every moment thou mayest be the intimate companion of that Kind Friend, and through fellowship with God become independent of association with His creatures. In all conditions, the heart that findeth intimacy with the eternal Beauty will not be disturbed by any terror, nor become sorrowful and disappointed from any estrangement.

order.why: Read a nearness that remoteness cannot affect.
shortened: Be not grieved by separation. A nearness hath been ordained for thee which no remoteness can affect. Verily, He is the Friend of him who hath detached himself in His love and turned to Him with a luminous countenance.

order.why: Consider separation by divine leave as a form of union.
shortened: Be not grieved by separation, for afterwards, by His command, that very separation was the essence of nearness, and parting by His leave was the reality of union.

order.why: Read the layered paradoxes of deprivation and attainment.
Keep the concise joining of distance and nearness.
shortened: For the substance of the grief is the essence of the visit, and the burning of the fire of zeal is the sweet water of the union. This distance is the nearness itself, this separation the reality of union.

order.why: Read separation as a key to union.
shortened: Praise be to God Who has made separation the key to union and remoteness the harbinger of nearness, Who has honored us with His oneness among His servants and adorned us with the ornament of His laws and ordinances.

order.why: Consider dispersion and wandering in the source’s consoling language.
Read the influence attributed to true spiritual union.
Hear the call to spiritual communion and fellowship.
shortened: When radiant faces gather together with watching eyes and penetrating insight, the desert of separation becomes the destination of reunion, and the season of separation reveals the bounties of union, and longing becomes the cause of burning passion.
Therefore, one must seek true nearness and spiritual communion and fellowship.

order.why: Consider the hope for nearness at the extremity of remoteness.
shortened: However, we hope that you, in the extremity of remoteness, may attain the utmost degree of nearness, and may drink and partake of the cup of the mysteries of God's Cause which until now hath been concealed from all souls, and may become firmly established and steadfast upon the sacred carpet.

order.why: Read the prayer for nearness that endures.
Keep the reassurance that follows sorrow at distance.
shortened: Sorrow not at remoteness, for God shall soon draw thee nigh unto Him.

order.why: Read the hope for reunion.
Hear the prayer to transform separation.
shortened: He said: We beseech God to protect and guard His honor Javad, upon him be peace, and to bestow upon him in every moment that which befits His generosity and bounty. Likewise we beseech God to transform the days of separation and remoteness into nearness and reunion.

order.why: Read the change from fire of separation to light of reunion.
Consider the images of honey, balm, and shore.
shortened: Thou shalt exchange the venom of separation for the honey of reunion, heal cruelty's blows with the balm of faith, hasten from the desert of remoteness unto the shore of nearness, and be set free from this dustbin of deprivation.

order.why: Hear the glad tidings that the time of remoteness has passed.
shortened: O assemblage of mystic knowers! Let your hearts be filled with joy, for the time of remoteness hath passed, and the spirit of certitude hath appeared, and the countenance of the celestial Youth hath beamed forth, adorned with the ornament of holiness in the paradise of His name, the Almighty.

order.why: Read the prayer for tranquility and joy through divine remembrance.
shortened: Let Thine everlasting melodies breathe tranquillity on me, O my Companion, and let the riches of Thine ancient countenance deliver me from all except Thee, O my Master, and let the tidings of the revelation of Thine incorruptible Essence bring me joy, O Thou Who art the most manifest of the manifest and the most hidden of the hidden!

order.why: Enter the extended invocation of love, hope, and nearness.
shortened: O Thou Whose face is the object of my adoration, Whose beauty is my sanctuary, Whose habitation is my goal, Whose praise is my hope, Whose providence is my companion, Whose love is the cause of my being, Whose mention is my solace, Whose nearness is my desire, Whose presence is my dearest wish and highest aspiration, I entreat Thee not to withhold from me the things Thou didst ordain for the chosen ones among Thy servants.

order.why: Keep the parallel prayer in its own source wording.
shortened: O Thou Whose face is the object of my adoration, Whose beauty is my sanctuary, Whose court is my goal, Whose remembrance is my wish, Whose affection is my solace, Whose love is my begetter, Whose praise is my companion, Whose nearness is my hope, Whose presence is my greatest longing and supreme aspiration!

order.why: Read nearness as joy and remembrance as companionship.
Allow loneliness and longing their full voice in prayer.
Hear the cry to end consuming separation.
Read the plea to abide within the divine court.
shortened: Suffer me, O my God, to draw nigh unto Thee, and to abide within the precincts of Thy court, for remoteness from Thee hath well-nigh consumed me.

order.why: Keep the image of hearts consumed by separation.
shortened: Some have attained His presence, while others yearn for it from afar. The fire of separation hath consumed hearts, and the flame of remoteness from the Ancient Beauty hath melted both horizons and souls.

order.why: Read the particular servant’s suffering and lamentation.
shortened: This is Thy servant who fashioned with his own hands what he fashioned for Thee, then was afflicted after that with separation and remoteness from Thee, whereby patience departed from all who have eyes to see, and whereby arose the lamentations of those near unto Thee, then their crying, and the weeping of the believers, then their weeping.

order.why: Hear the prayer’s expression of apparent abandonment.
shortened: It is as though Thou hast forgotten him and left him in the wastelands of Thy separation and estrangement, and delivered him before the face of Thine enemies that they might do with him as they please and inflict upon him whatsoever they desire.

order.why: Consider the scattered gazelles as an image of longing.
shortened: They are the flock of Thy gazelles, wandering in the wilderness of separation and scattered in the valley of regret.

order.why: Read thirst in separation beside the fountain of life.
Keep the repeated invocation and question about attaining presence.
Read the appeal for assistance amid longing.
shortened: Assist me, O Thou through Whom the sincere ones have soared in the atmosphere of Thy nearness and reunion, and the hearts of the devoted ones have been consumed in their remoteness and separation from Thee.

order.why: Hear the prayer not to be kept from mercy’s ocean.
shortened: Suffer me not, I implore Thee, to be kept back from the ocean of Thy tender mercies, nor to be far removed from the shores of nearness to Thee.

order.why: Keep the petition for the shore of nearness.
shortened: Deprive me not in these days of the fragrant breezes of Thy contentment, nor from hearing the warbling of the Dove of Thy Cause. And distance me not, O my Beloved, from the shore of the ocean of Thy nearness and presence.

order.why: Join grace with the request not to be distanced.
Read the prayer for the servants’ access to nearness.
Keep the related petition for the seat of the Cause.
Read pardon and beneficence in the prayer for release from separation.
Ask for what draws loved ones near in every condition.
shortened: Send down, then, O my God, through Thy Most Great Name, upon Thy loved ones what will, under all conditions, draw them nearer unto Thee.

order.why: Contrasts divine nearness with remoteness from human comprehension.
Retain the personal request for nearness in all circumstances.
shortened: I beseech Thee, O Thou Who art the Possessor of existence and the Forgiver of sins, by the lights of Thy countenance through which the Sun of Thy bounty hath shone upon existence, and by Thy Most Great Name which hath encompassed the world, to assist me to be steadfast in Thy Cause in such wise that neither the oppression of tyrants nor the injustice of pharaohs may frighten me. Then write down for me that which will draw me nigh unto Thee in all conditions.

order.why: Read the movement from self toward divine bounty.
shortened: O Lord! I am the one who has fled from myself unto Thee and desired from the heaven of Thy bounty what befits Thy grace and Thy bestowal. Verily Thou art He Whom the affairs of creation cannot frustrate, so send down upon Thy servant from the heaven of Thy grace that which will draw him near unto Thee in all conditions.

order.why: Hear the prayer directed toward the Kaaba of presence.
shortened: O my Lord! I am he who hath turned towards Thee and sought the Kaaba of Thy presence and the horizon of Thy reunion.

order.why: Follow the prayer’s many images of turning, refuge, and communion.
Read hope for the grace given to those freed from imagined idols.
shortened: O Lord! Thou seest me turning toward Thee and hoping for that which lieth with Thee. I beseech Thee not to disappoint me of that which hath been ordained by the Most Exalted Pen for Thy chosen servants who have, through Thy power and might, shattered the idols of vain imaginings and idle fancies.

order.why: Keep the request not to be left to oneself.
Read longing for the horizon of grace.
shortened: Grant, moreover, that they whose hearts yearn over Thee may draw nigh unto the horizon of Thy grace, above which the Day-Star of Thy beauty sheddeth its radiance.

order.why: Consider the attraction of holy melodies in the prayer.
Keep the thanksgiving for guidance, renewed life, and removed veils.
shortened: Therefore, raise thy hands in supplication and need toward the court of the Peerless Lord and offer prayers and praise, saying: "O Lord, O Creator! Thou hast given this weak ant a place on the carpet of the Solomon of the divine realm, guided this lost one to the shore of the ocean of Thy oneness, quenched this thirsty one with the Salsabil of bounty, brought this dead one to life with the spirit of eternal life, illumined this dejected face, and burned away these thick veils.

order.why: Hear the assurance that yearning has been heard.
Read the gaze of providence toward a particular direction.
shortened: The Glance of Divine Providence has ever been turned towards that direction.

order.why: Keep the assurance of remembrance in the Holy Court.
Consider remembrance and revealed verses as a means of drawing near.
shortened: We give thee glad tidings of My remembrance and recite unto thee My verses and draw thee nigh unto My mighty Kingdom.

order.why: Read the particular mention of Haydar and the prayer for him.
shortened: And We make mention of him who hath been named Haydar from the direction of My Most Luminous Horizon, that he may draw nigh unto God, the One, the Single, the All-Hearing, the All-Seeing.

order.why: Keep the blessing on attaining the lights of the Countenance.
Read the personal address to Muhammad about divine favors.
shortened: O Muhammad! Thou hast attained unto divine favors and reached the sacred station of nearness.

order.why: Consider recognition after others have turned away.
Read the blessing on turning toward the illumined horizon.
Read gratitude for nearness to the Blessed Tree.
Keep the particular family’s recognition in the source’s own terms.
Distinguish walking with the feet from turning with the spirit.
Read the passionate wanderer’s search for rest.
shortened: For some time there was no news of you in the visible world. Some said you had taken residence in the monastery, while others pointed to the mosque saying you had secluded yourself there. I said this bewildered, passionate one finds rest nowhere but in the divine sanctuary, and this wanderer of separation takes seclusion nowhere but in the Lord's Ka'bah.

order.why: Consider the heart’s rest, the eye’s tranquility, and the soul’s repose.
Read shelter as attraction to divine beauty.
shortened: If thou seekest eternal rest take shelter beneath the protection of God's Beauty and if thou seekest everlasting gifts enter beneath the shade of His loving providence and bounty. This protection and providence, this shade of bounty is none other than attraction to the holy fragrances of His divine Beauty.

order.why: Keep the fortress and palace images.
shortened: If you seek an impregnable fortress, seek the shadow of the Glorious Lord. If you desire a lofty palace, seek the seat of truth with the All-Powerful Sovereign.

order.why: Consider solace within the paradise of loving-kindness.
Hear the invitation to security and fellowship.
Read the journey from the west of remoteness to the east of nearness.
shortened: Yet we hope that a breeze of grace may waft over you and draw you from the west of remoteness to the east of nearness, that you may find repose in the eternal holy Ridvan in the company of the holy manifestations of divine fellowship.

order.why: Follow the movement beyond fancy and limitation toward attraction.
shortened: Perchance they will be attracted by this melody whereby were attracted the spirits of the near ones among the dwellers of the paradise of the most high, and will journey from the worlds of fancy to the sanctuaries of holiness, and will migrate from the abodes of limitations to the treasuries of eternity, that they may arrive at the stream of nearness and attainment and alight upon the shore of the sea of attraction and beauty.

order.why: Keep the imagery of ascent in the Tablet of the Hair.
shortened: It is calling aloud at all times upon the branch of Fire within the hallowed and luminous garden of Paradise, that perchance the inmates of the realm of creation may detach themselves from the world of dust and ascend unto the retreats of nearness -- the Spot where the Fire seeketh illumination from the light of the Countenance of God, the Glorious, the Powerful.

order.why: Read the Bird’s detachment as a sign of nearness.
Consider the invitation to pass beyond place.
Keep the image of two bow-lengths or less.
shortened: Then grant him that which will cause him to ascend unto the stations of nearness, "the distance of two bow-lengths or even less."

order.why: Read the aspiration to spiritual connection while living on earth.
shortened: May ye reach such a condition and attain such a station that though ye dwell upon the earth ye are at all times intimately connected to the Concourse on High. Though your bodies live and move down here upon the dust let your spirits soar into the realms of Abha and behold its lights.

order.why: Consider the heart’s swift ascent in the source’s imagery.
Keep the invitation to companionship in the Abha Kingdom.
Read the imagery of loftiness and the divine Court.
shortened: This loftiness dwells in the divine Court, and this height resides in the Most Great Throne of the All-Merciful. All existence and being lie at the depths of this summit and height, and all loftiness and grandeur exist under the shade of this heavenly exaltation.

order.why: Consider nearness as everlasting bounty.
Read the Bab’s prayer relating paradise and fire to nearness and remoteness.
Keep the account of being veiled as a spiritual torment.
shortened: The other kind of torment is palpable and consists in physical punishments such as imprisonment, beating, expulsion and banishment. But for the people of God, to be veiled from Him is still more grievous than all these torments.

order.why: Join the meanings of heaven and hell with thoughts, purposes, and deeds.
shortened: Good thoughts, good resolves, and good deeds bring men nearer to God, and that is heaven. Hell is the state of mind in which there are evil thoughts and purposes, yielding to the desires of the senses, clinging to material things. In that state man is separated from God, and in his ignorance he suffers.

order.why: Read the reported experience of divine bounty in turning toward God.
Consider the paired movement toward light and away from darkness.
shortened: The nearer you are to the light, the further you are from the darkness; the nearer you are to heaven, the further you are from the earth; the nearer you are to God, the further you are from the world.

order.why: Ask what draws near and what alienates.
Read commandments and prohibitions in relation to nearness.
Consider the purpose attributed to divine commands.
Read the reference to drawing near in its context of following a departed believer’s conduct.
shortened: Although letters have been sent in Arabic, Persian and all kinds of ways, nevertheless love is expressed anew that you should, God willing, follow that departed one in all matters pertaining to the material world. This will surely be the nearest means of drawing nigh unto God.

order.why: Keep the assurance about what is desired for the recipient.
shortened: Be not grieved by exile, for God hath made it a means of drawing thee nearer to thy Lord. He desireth for thee naught save that which shall draw thee closer to thy Lord, the Mighty, the All-Forgiving.

order.why: Read the invitation to the court as a mirror of beauty.
shortened: He desireth for no one save that which will draw him nigh unto the sacred court, the station wherein whosoever entereth will behold himself as a mirror of His beauty, the Mighty, the Wondrous.

order.why: Hear the stated purpose of the summons toward God.
Read that summons across successive ages.
shortened: Rather, in all successive ages and consecutive days, the entire creation from the beginning that has no beginning has been commanded to turn to this Source of glorious bounty, and the divine Herald has ever called and will continue to call the servants from estrangement in transient, passing homelands to draw near to the glorious, eternal abodes.

order.why: Consider the bestowal that draws earth’s people near.
Ask for assistance to remove hindering veils.
shortened: We beseech God that He may assist thee to rend asunder the veils that have hindered thee, with celestial power, that thou mayest attain to the station of nearness and holiness.

order.why: Join seeing, hearing, turning, and contemplating.
shortened: Today all must speak for the sake of God and gaze toward God. Let them not deprive their eyes from the supreme horizon, nor prevent their ears from hearkening to the words of the Lord of Names, nor withhold their hearts from turning to Him, nor veil their minds from contemplating His mighty signs and manifest conditions.

order.why: Consider the contrast between turning and heedlessness.
shortened: Whoever turned attained their portion and share, and whoever remained heedless was deprived and distant. Blessed are they, men and women, who have turned, and woe to them, men and women, who are heedless.

order.why: Read the counsel to remain attentive amid others’ forgetfulness.
Consider firmness that cannot be displaced from nearness.
Keep the blessing on holding fast to the cord.
shortened: The glory be upon thee and upon those who have soared in the atmosphere of My nearness and held fast to My strong cord.

order.why: Read loving-kindness and turning with the heart together.
Hear the invitation to connect the heart to the Ocean.
shortened: Strive to connect thy heart to the Most Great Ocean. In this way, the divine bounty will ever encompass thee.

order.why: Join nearness of heart with gladness of spirit.
Consider good-pleasure as the heart’s desire.
shortened: O Javad! The heart's desire of every person of understanding is to increase in nearness to the Divine Threshold, and the wish of every wise one is to attain the good-pleasure of the Most Glorious Beauty, may my spirit be a sacrifice for His loved ones.

order.why: Read fidelity to good-pleasure as a path toward reunion.
Keep the prayer’s detachment in its own devotional voice.
shortened: When we attained unto Thy nearness, we did sever ourselves from kith and kin alike, desiring only to know Thee, to praise Thee and to worship Thee.

order.why: Consider enduring gifts alongside the passing character of earthly glory.
shortened: In the estimation of the loved ones of God, abasement is exaltation itself, and affliction leadeth to faithfulness. Earthly glory and comfort are but a mirage of illusion, while in the realm of the spirit heavenly gifts are everlasting and imperishable. The lights in the nether world may be bright, but they are put out at the break of dawn, whereas the stars that shine in the heaven of the love of God will sparkle continually throughout ages and centuries. Such is everlasting glory, such is infinite bounty, such is life eternal, and such is boundless grace.

order.why: Read growth in radiance and steadfastness.
Keep the hope for daily spiritual progress.
shortened: I hope therefore that at the Divine Threshold thou mayest secure favor, may become connected with the Kingdom by ideal ties and may daily progress so that thou mayest be accepted in the Sight of His Holiness Baha'u'llah!

order.why: Consider desire for nearness as a source of continuing progress.
Hear the appeal for a fresh bounty each day.
Read the reported love of children and their nearness to the Kingdom.
Consider spiritual brotherhood as a movement toward nearness.
shortened: This spiritual brotherhood has no other purpose than nearness to the Threshold of God.

order.why: Keep the allusion to drawing near through voluntary devotion.
Read the image of divine response exceeding the first human step.
shortened: When man turns to God, He says "Whosoever draws nigh unto Me by a span, I will draw nigh unto him by a cubit." This means that any servant who comes closer to Me by one span, I will come closer to him by one cubit. The purpose is that the slightest turning of man toward God becomes the cause of infinite nearness.

order.why: Connect that image specifically with guiding souls and attracting hearts.
shortened: In the sacred hadith He says: "Whoso draweth nigh unto Me a span, I draw nigh unto him a cubit." This drawing nigh is through the guidance of souls and the attraction of hearts.

order.why: Consider servitude as the wings of nearness.
shortened: In the contingent world, even unto the very acme of the Placeless, loftiness, advancement and exaltation are impossible save on the wings of servitude; while nearness to the Holy Presence is unattainable unless the pinions of thraldom be unfurled.

order.why: Read service as a means of drawing close.
Follow nearness into giving fresh life to hearts.
Close by joining service, love, remembrance, and turning toward God.
shortened: Blessed is he who hath arisen to serve His Cause, who hath attained unto the cup of His love, who hath spoken in His remembrance and praise, who hath turned toward Him with his heart, who hath stood in His court, and who hath circled round His throne.

questions: What changes when nearness is understood as a quality of relationship rather than physical distance?
How do the sunlight and polished-surface images help explain spiritual receptivity, and what remains beyond their reach?
What do the prayers allow a person to express about loneliness, longing, and hope?
How does the Qur’anic account of prayer and response illuminate the movement toward nearness described here?
How are good thoughts, deeds, and service connected with the language of heaven, companionship, and reunion?
What practices could deepen spiritual presence and responsibility when outward circumstances keep people apart?

references.label: 1 · Qur’an 2:186 · Nearness, prayer, and response
references.note: Read the assurance of divine nearness and response to prayer alongside the invitation for people to respond and believe. Compare this relationship of calling and answering with the compilation’s prayers and its movement from longing toward action. Consider also how its philosophical passages qualify spatial language about God.

subjects.displayTitle: Human capacity: difference, dignity, and development
subjects.introduction: Bahá’u’lláh asks no one to measure their vessel against a neighbour’s; the whole duty of a soul is to fill its own with the grace poured out for it. That counsel does not deny that people differ. ‘Abdu’l-Bahá speaks plainly of minds unequal in capacity, of ten children in one school with ten degrees of understanding, of a shell no polishing will turn into a pearl. Yet He insists just as plainly that human beings are intrinsically equal as the countless waves of the sea are one water, no one may be treated with contempt, and no one may be denied an education. The eye is finer than the nail, but the body could not be all eye, and Paul’s picture of members that need one another makes the same point [1]. What can an educator know of a child, and what must stay open to discovery? The questions lead on into the development of capacity, into education as the unfolding of hidden gifts, and into a divine grace that shines on every mirror alike while asking each to be polished.
subjects.arc: Begin with dignity and shared belonging, explore the meanings and limits of difference, examine education and receptivity, and return to the responsibility to cultivate gifts without contempt.

order.why: Open by shifting attention from comparison to receiving one’s portion.
shortened: The whole duty of man in this Day is to attain that share of the flood of grace which God poureth forth for him. Let none, therefore, consider the largeness or smallness of the receptacle. The portion of some might lie in the palm of a man’s hand, the portion of others might fill a cup, and of others even a gallon-measure.

order.why: Establish the explicit affirmation of intrinsic human equality.
Read the rejection of contempt and the obligation to educate and heal.
Keep education open to every member of the human family.
Consider diverse capacity as a reason for unity.
shortened: As difference in degree of capacity exists among human souls, as difference in capability is found, therefore, individualities will differ one from another. But in reality this is a reason for unity and not for discord and enmity. If the flowers of a garden were all of one color, the effect would be monotonous to the eye; but if the colors are variegated, it is most pleasing and wonderful.

order.why: Introduce the interdependence of eye and nail.
Acknowledge what educators do not know about inherent capacity.
shortened: In training mankind we must especially keep in mind: 1. The inherent capacity of an individual, the hereditary factor, is an unknown entity for the educator and teacher. 2. Not quite so obscure and mysterious are the moulding powers of the environment in which man grows up, in which he - according to the decree of God - was born.

order.why: Question the expectation that everyone possess every perfection.
Read equality before the divine call.
Keep the parallel account of equal placement before the Manifestation.
shortened: Indeed, had they known Him through His own Self or by virtue of that which He hath revealed, they would not have repudiated Him when He appeared in this glorious and incomparable Name, which God hath ordained to be the Sword of His Revelation between heaven and earth, and through which truth is separated from error, even from now until the Day when mankind shall stand before the Lord of the worlds. Know thou moreover that in the Day of His Manifestation all created things besides God shall be brought forth and placed equally, irrespective of their rank being high or low.

order.why: Distinguish this initial equality from different responses.
shortened: At the time of the Revelation all men are equal in rank. By reason, however, of their acceptance or rejection, rise or fall, motion or stillness, recognition or denial, they come to differ thereafter. For instance, the one true God, magnified be His glory, speaking through the intermediary of His Manifestation, doth ask: "Am I not your Lord?" Every soul that answereth "Yea, verily!" is accounted among the most distinguished of all men in the sight of God.

order.why: Consider the shared created nature affirmed here.
Read original purity alongside the acquisition of virtues and vices.
shortened: Know thou that every soul is fashioned after the nature of God, each being pure and holy at his birth. Afterwards, however, the individuals will vary according to what they acquire of virtues or vices in this world. Although all existent beings are in their very nature created in ranks or degrees, for capacities are various, nevertheless every individual is born holy and pure, and only thereafter may he become defiled.

order.why: Consider the range of attributes found in human beings.
shortened: Moreover, knowledge is a human attribute but so is ignorance; truthfulness is a human attribute but so is falsehood; and the same holds true of trustworthiness and treachery, justice and tyranny, and so forth. In brief, every perfection and virtue, as well as every vice, is an attribute of man.

order.why: Keep distinctions of conduct separate from claims of identity between God and creation.
Read the mirror of all divine names and the particular prominence of one.
Consider different reflections of a single creative Word.
Read common creation and varied soils together.
Consider variation of opinion in the account of existence.
shortened: It is clear that human realities differ one from another, that opinions and perceptions vary, and that this divergence of thoughts, opinions, understandings and sentiments among individuals is an essential requirement. For differences of degree in creation are among the essential requirements of existence, which is resolved into countless forms.

order.why: Explore the potter’s diverse forms and their distinct perfections.
Keep harmony and perfection in each degree together.
Ask what would be lost in a world of identical ages and capacities.
Read the variety of flowers as a further image.
Consider the reported connection between difference and appreciation.
Read the account of differences in circumstances and moral qualities.
shortened: From an economic standpoint in the law of living there is a great deal of difference. Some are poor, others wealthy; some are wise, others ignorant; some are patient and serene, some impatient and excitable; some are prone to justice, others practice injustice and oppression; some are meek, others arrogant. In brief, there are many points of distinction among humankind.

order.why: Consider the source’s argument about degrees and material inequality.
shortened: It is not meant that all will be equal, for inequality in degree and capacity is a property of nature.

order.why: Read the account of ranks beside its insistence on rights and the common welfare.
Keep the military analogy and its argument about intelligence attributed to this report.
Read the related comparison between commanders and soldiers.
Return to the distinct tasks of eye and nail.
shortened: When we consider god has made a stone to be a stone, man to be a man, etc., can we say god has shown oppression to a stone, because it is not a man? God has given according to capacity. He has created men with nails and eyes. Can nails say, "I am oppressed because I am not the eye? Can the foot say, "O, God, Thou hast not shown Mercy because I am not the brain?" God has given according to station.

order.why: Consider professional aptitude and the example of misplaced occupation.
Read aptitude in writing, teaching, and leadership.
Ask what it means to avoid forcing a child into an unsuitable field.
shortened: For a child will sooner or later make manifest his natural abilities and gifts. To train his natural abilities in a manner different from this is not right. For it has often been found that certain parents forced their child to study a certain line desired by them for which, however, the child had not natural aptitude. Thus the child lavished years of his life in that line, with no progress whatever. This shows that the child's abilities were adapted to some other line of study.

order.why: Consider the reported contrast between scholarship and business success.
Read the preference for developing qualities over seeking office.
Introduce education as the unfolding of potential.
shortened: That is to say, education cannot alter the inner essence of a man, but it doth exert tremendous influence, and with this power it can bring forth from the individual whatever perfections and capacities are deposited within him.
Thus is it clearly demonstrated that by their essential nature, minds vary as to their capacity, while education also playeth a great role and exerteth a powerful effect on their development.

order.why: Read the observation of differences among children.
Examine the reported dispute over education and innate capacity.
shortened: It is evident that although education improves the morals of mankind, confers the advantages of civilization and elevates man from lowest degrees to the station of sublimity, there is, nevertheless, a difference in the intrinsic or natal capacity of individuals. Ten children of the same age, with equal station of birth, taught in the same school, partaking of the same food, in all respects subject to the same environment, their interests equal and in common, will evidence separate and distinct degrees of capability and advancement; some will be exceedingly intelligent and progressive, some of mediocre ability, others limited and incapable.

order.why: Read the full question and answer on character, retaining its historical explanations of inheritance.
shortened: Answer: There are the innate character, the inherited character, and the acquired character, which is gained through education.

As to the innate character, although the innate nature bestowed by God upon man is purely good, yet that character differs among men according to the degrees they occupy: All degrees are good, but some are more so than others. Thus every human being possesses intelligence and capacity, but intelligence, capacity, and aptitude differ from person to person. This is self-evident.

For example, take a number of children from the same place and family, attending the same school and instructed by the same teacher, raised on the same food and in the same climate, wearing the same clothing and studying the same lessons: It is certain that among these children some will become skilled in the arts and sciences, some will be of average ability, and some will be dull. It is therefore clear that in man's innate nature there is a difference in degree, aptitude, and capacity, but it is not a matter of good or evil---it is merely a difference of degree.

As to differences in inherited character, they arise from the strength and weakness of man's constitution; that is, if the parents are of weak constitution, then the children will be likewise, and if they are strong, then the children will also be robust.

order.why: Distinguish individuality from acquired personality in the mirror analogy.
shortened: Personality is of two kinds. One is the natural or God-given personality which the western thinkers call individuality, the inner aspect of man which is not subject to change; and the other personality is the result of acquired arts, sciences and virtues with which man is decorated.

As regards the personality which is the result of acquired virtues, let us take this mirror as an example: In the beginning it was a piece of black stone; now, through the process of purification, it has become a mirror and has reflecting power and displays its innate perfections so that they are clearly visible to all. The rock was endowed with a distinct individuality which acquired a personality through the process of education.

order.why: Read environment and growth within the account of individuality.
shortened: Owing to environment, soul-needs differ; rich and poor, wise and ignorant, etc. Environment has its dark side and its light side. Development has its good aspects and bad aspects.

Each soul has its station of individuality in which it may develop itself, but a soul cannot leave its own station for another station or individuality. Man accomplishes his true growth when the soul develops in its own station. His station does not change; simply his capacity for knowing God is increased and developed.

order.why: Consider innate and acquired qualities together.
Keep the reported three degrees of children’s capacities attributed to its source.
shortened: In beings there are degrees; all are not in the same station. Observe the various characters to be seen and compared, say, among ten children who have received identically the same treatment, training and food. Three degrees will be found, which might be classes as, rapid development, less rapid, and almost stagnant.

order.why: Read the educator’s garden analogy.
Join innate development with education and effort.
Consider the need for education suited to children’s capacities.
shortened: That child has capacity - if he is properly educated he will achieve success and prosperity in the future.

order.why: Read the explicit counsel to adapt education.
shortened: O thou who art firm in the verses of God! Just as a tailor examines the form and stature when considering cloth and garments of silk and wool, and cuts and tailors the clothing according to the figure, likewise those who bestow the garment of knowledge and understanding and sew the robe of guidance must consider capacity, capability and worthiness, and accordingly arrange the garment of education and the shirt of guidance, clothing therewith the form of search and the reality of receptive and attentive souls.

order.why: Consider the child’s capacity to learn scientific truths.
Read the report about readiness for teaching at different ages.
Distinguish the source’s accounts of childhood simplicity and mature strength.
shortened: This is the difference between the perfect man and the child. Both have the underlying qualities of simplicity and sincerity -- the child through the power of weakness and the man through the power of strength.

order.why: Question age as a sufficient measure of wisdom.
Keep the second comparison of young wisdom and older ignorance.
Read the severe estimate of a child’s learning capacity as a particular historical report.
shortened: Now there is a child who cannot remember things. It has no mind, no power of understanding. However much it may progress, it will not become like an intelligent person.

order.why: Explore the call to train capacity through the images of light, oil, and appetite.
Read children, illness, and ignorance in the account of educational responsibility.
Consider choice and circumstance through warp and weft, retaining the source omission.
Read the development of rational individuality in relation to bodily life.
shortened: The rational soul is endowed from the beginning with individuality; it does not acquire it through the intermediary of the body. At most, what can be said is that the individuality and identity of the rational soul may be strengthened in this world, and that it may either progress and attain to the degrees of perfection or remain in the lowest abyss of ignorance and be veiled from and deprived of beholding the signs of God.

order.why: Consider the continuation of distinctions beyond death.
shortened: Observe that when spirits are attached to bodies, they are distinguished from each other in all aspects - some at the highest level of perception and perfection, others at the lowest degree of deficiency and abasement. Similarly, after their return to divine realms, this distinction and differentiation continues to exist.

order.why: Read the reported diversity of attainments in the next world.
shortened: [The questioner remarked that many differing opinions were held as to the conditions of the future life. Some thought that all would have exactly the same perfections and virtues; that all would be equal and alike.]
Abdu'l-Baha said there would be variety, and differing degrees of attainment, as in this world.

order.why: Keep relative nonexistence distinct from annihilation.
shortened: Thou hast written that some of the friends have informed thee that if man does not progress, he will perish and become nonexistent. What is intended is not absolute nonexistence. The meaning is that the existence of a heedless person in comparison to the existence of a perfect individual is like being nonexistent. For instance, a stone is nonexistent in comparison to man, even though it existeth in the mineral condition. In brief, all souls exist, but the existence of the heedless and the ignorant in comparison to the existence of the perfect and the wise is like nonexistence.

order.why: Read the limits of gnat and sparrow as the source’s analogies.
shortened: Who hath the power to soar in that exalted atmosphere or to cherish another beloved than Him? We all abide beneath His shadow and seek our portion from the ocean of His grace. However far the gnat may fly, it can never traverse the length and breadth of heaven, and however high the sparrow may soar, it can never attain the tree of immortality.

order.why: Consider the mine and its different materials.
Read fitness through the contrasting nest and house.
Keep the comparison between a child’s understanding and heavenly knowledge in context.
Read the question and answer about the capacity of hearers of the Manifestations.
Consider repeated meanings addressed to different capacities.
Read the counsel to speak with forbearance according to the hearer.
shortened: It behooveth the people of God to be forbearing. They should impart the Word of God according to the hearer’s particular measure of understanding and capacity, that perchance the children of men may be roused from heedlessness and set their faces towards this Horizon which is immeasurably exalted above every horizon.

order.why: Explore accommodation through the example of a father and infant.
Keep the concise joining of capacity and circumstance.
Consider the source’s explanation of differing laws.
Read the reported contrast between specialized knowledge and another person’s understanding.
shortened: Those men around them who heard their voice were those who were capable and desirous of hearing them.

If you speak with a magician about the Zodiac he understands you because he is a learned man; but if you speak of it to a carpenter, he will say it is nonsense, " How is it, a live man in the heavens!

order.why: Connect adaptation of speech with meeting need and avoiding antagonism.
Consider the contrast between swift understanding and a long visit.
Allow for fruit that ripens at different rates.
shortened: Good people are of two kinds,- those who are so by natural goodness of heart, and those who attain to it by an after gift of the Spirit. All those who are truly taught of God, will accept this Truth when presented to them, but as it takes some fruits longer to ripen than others, so some will accept it immediately, and others after a long time of gradually ripening in the Sun.

order.why: Read differences in response to counsel.
shortened: One man may be highly sensitized and responds quickly to all advices and exhortations but another may need sharper measures.

order.why: Consider the reported plurality of paths of individual development.
Explore rivers and valleys as images of differing capacity.
Keep the companion image of rivers and light.
Ask how both large and small vessels may receive truth.
shortened: The capacities of men differ. If you pour water into two vessels, a large and a small one, though both may be filled one will contain more water than the other. So of men-one may have more truth than another; but the one who has less, may still have truth.

order.why: Read the ocean and each person’s thirst.
Consider appetite at the table in the reported reference to Christ.
shortened: Thus Christ spread the table of his spiritual food and called a great number of people in order to take their portions. Out of these only eleven came and attended the table. And these eleven, how did it happen that they gained from the blessing? It was because they had desired to come and take. They had the appetite!

order.why: Read diminished appetite through the source’s illness analogy.
Keep the nightingale, beetle, and cow as figurative comparisons of attraction.
Read the related bat and beetle imagery without turning it into a judgment of particular people.
shortened: In brief, O loved ones of God, though the bounty is infinite, what spiritual benefit or physical gain can come to those who waste it? They are utterly deprived, forbidden, despairing, rejected, tormented and subdued. What fault lies with the morning light if the night-blind bat seeks no shelter save the cavity of endless doubts? What blame attaches to the holy fragrances if the dung beetle finds no pleasure in sweet scents and its nostrils remain unperfumed?

order.why: Distinguish the constancy of the Spirit from variation in reception.
Consider how the sun remains unaffected by its mirrors.
shortened: Were unnumbered mirrors to be placed before it, each would, according to its capacity, reflect the splendor of that sun, and were none to be placed before it, it would still continue to rise and set, and the mirrors alone would be veiled from its light.

order.why: Read the sun’s universal shining and the preparation of the mirror.
shortened: Consider how all are recipients of the bounty of the same Sun. At most the difference between them is that of degree, for the effulgence is one effulgence, the one light emanating from the Sun.

One heart may possess the capacity of the polished mirror; another, be covered and obscured by the dust and dross of this world. Although the same Sun is shining upon both, in the mirror which is polished, pure and sanctified you may behold the Sun in all its fullness, glory and power, revealing its majesty and effulgence; but in the mirror which is rusted and obscured there is no capacity for reflection, although so far as the Sun itself is concerned it is shining thereon and is neither lessened nor deprived.

order.why: Explore the varied effects in crystal.
shortened: Some possessed a pure reality and were recipients of these universal outpourings, and like luminous crystal the heat of the Sun so influenced their essential nature that they acquired the heat of the ether. Others received but a reflection and a ray, while some were entirely deprived.

order.why: Consider the breeze and the condition of its recipient.
shortened: There are two kinds of animate beings. One kind feels the breeze, and receives its benefit as it is passing. The other kind, though in the breeze, receives no breeze therefrom. The more healthy one is (in a good, spiritual condition), the greater will be the benefit.

order.why: Keep the Manifestation’s disclosure distinct from differences in perception.
shortened: God is to every human being as great as the individual mental capacity permits one to see Him. So, also, is the Manifestation who represents Him in this world of beings. Each individual perceives with the faculties peculiar to his own evolution. The Manifestation appeared not for a few, but for all. To the simple, as to the great, he is the same: but some see him in one light, some in another, according to their capacities to perceive.

order.why: Read one Day, Light, and Call alongside varied responses.
shortened: And the Day was one and the Light was one and the Manifestation was one and the Call was one, yet souls were at great variance and creation was in ranks differing from each other by a straight line.

order.why: Consider presence and absence beyond physical attendance.
Read the contrast between a single call and a cannon through its material analogies.
shortened: You find a man will be wakened by a single call. Another is never quickened even if you discharge a cannon! As soon as the ray of the sun shines through crystal it will burn, but if the same ray fall on a stone, no effect is produced.

order.why: Consider readiness that responds without an outward word.
Read dry wood, wet wood, and stone as images of receptivity.
Keep the parallel imagery of hearing and ignition in its own source terms.
shortened: As for him whose vision hath deviated and whose ears God hath covered with deafness, he findeth no trace of this.
Signs and warnings profit not - stone and clay are hardly set ablaze by the heat of sparks.

order.why: Read the concise image of rocks that do not ignite.
Consider the source’s use of sensory deprivation as a spiritual metaphor.
Retain the companion metaphor without treating it as a claim about disabled people’s spiritual lives.
shortened: The blind are deprived of beholding the light of the sun, the deaf receive no share of hearing the melody of the Concourse on High.

order.why: Keep the sharp figurative contrast between moon and cattle attributed to its source.
shortened: Though both appear in human form, one is like the moon and the other like cattle - such is the difference that exists within the human species!

order.why: Read the image of vegetation and receptive ground.
shortened: As for the good earth, the blessed soil - it brought forth its vegetation by the leave of its Lord. But that which is corrupt bringeth forth naught but that which is worthless.

order.why: Compare good soil and rock.
Consider salt earth and the scriptural allusion to being chosen.
Read the relation between outpouring and receptivity.
shortened: These universal outpourings which illuminate and encompass all directions, lighting up East and West - their radiance had no effect on the eyes of the blind, their sweet fragrance did not perfume any nostrils, their wondrous bounty yielded no fruit for the ignorant soul, their precious gift gave no benefit to the base person.

order.why: Keep continuing bounty beside human acceptance.
shortened: This being the case, no argument remains for the remote one against the Absolute Bestower, for according to his own acceptance and seeking has he settled in that station. Otherwise, there is no suspension in the bounty of the Generous One, no cause for distancing from the source of bounty and generosity, no aversion of the Creator from the created without reason.

order.why: Consider boundless bounty received in differing measure.
Read the concise statement about receiving according to capacity.
Consider each portion in relation to virtue.
shortened: Thou hast, also, assigned unto every soul a portion of this virtue in accordance with the Tablet of Thy decree and the Scriptures of Thine irrevocable judgment.

order.why: Read capacity to hear a claim concerning divinity.
shortened: How can one who is disturbed by mention of divine authority be capable of bearing mention of divinity? Souls who considered themselves among the mighty ones and learned of the Bayan were struck down by mention of divinity - how much more so those souls who were raised in the Dispensation of the Furqan and were afflicted for centuries at the hands of the divines of idle fancy.

order.why: Keep the account of stations concealed from limited capacity.
Consider the reversals of rising and falling.
Read the contrast between learned or powerful people and those who attain.
Keep the companion reversal between poor people and princes.
shortened: How many a prince turned away from the Truth and deprived himself of the Most Great Joy which appeared with manifest sovereignty! And how many a poor one heard and hastened until he reached the shore of the ocean of divine knowledge, from whose waves can be heard: "There is none other God but Him, the All-Knowing, the All-Informed."

order.why: Read the springs of certainty in their particular account of companions.
shortened: Souls are diverse: some drink from the pure water of certitude while being detached and independent of all other waters of the earth, while others drink from different springs, and these springs too are various. Consider the Companions of the Apostle of God - may the spirit of all else but Him be sacrificed for His sake. Some were at the highest pinnacle of faith and assurance, while others would at times ascend and at times descend.

order.why: Consider faith and certitude in the reference to women and men.
Distinguish blameless differences of degree from the source’s moral evaluation of faith.
Read the reported interpretation of emotional fluctuation without making it a general diagnosis.
shortened: In short, an infinitesimal incident gives happiness to some, and the most inconsequential event makes others sad. In the morning, they are boiling over with the exuberance of joyousness, and in the evening, they have simmered down to the point of despondency and sheer disappointment. This is a sign of the weakness of their characters and the feebleness of their faith.

order.why: Let the account of faith as a gift challenge an assumption of earned worthiness.
shortened: O thou who art illumined by the Sun of Guidance! Every bounty is possible to be bestowed according to capacity, worthiness, merit and capability, except the bounty of faith and certitude which is purely a gift and solely a bestowal, and is among those things pertaining to "He singles out for His mercy whomsoever He pleases."

order.why: Consider gifts requested and gifts already received.
shortened: There are certain gifts which God grants after request. There are others which God grants without request.

The Lord gave us the eye without our seeking it, for he gave it to us in the matrix of the mother, and there we were not conscious of any supplication for it. He conferred upon us hearing without our seeking it. All the parts and members of the human organism were given it without its asking for them.

order.why: Read trustworthiness as a capacity that bears fruit through wisdom.
shortened: Not every heart is capable of acting as a repository for divine love. For not every soul is suited for growing wondrous herbs--only the heart of a human being who continues to bear the trustworthiness of the All-Merciful and to give the fruit of wisdom and eloquence.

order.why: Consider divers returning with mud or pearls as an image of seeking.
shortened: The people of the world are all divers, they plunge in the deep ocean of existence. Most of them when submerged bring out a few shells filled with mud; whereas others bring out with them peerless pearls.

order.why: Read praise in the Tablets as an address to potential still to be realized.
Connect happiness with developing hidden powers of thought and love.
shortened: But the unfoldment of human happiness depends upon the exercise of the hidden functions of intellect. It is through the Love of God, the Knowledge of God, the spiritual susceptibilities, and the attractions of the heart.

order.why: Explains the need for a unifying power amid differences of understanding and capacity.
Return to the Spirit’s unifying influence amid different thoughts.
Read Plotinus’s distinct account of sufficiency and comparison.
Keep the supplied education excerpt with its omissions visible.
shortened: It is certain that human beings are, by their very nature, different one from the other.... the disparity among individuals is due to differences of degree which are innate. But the Manifestations also consider that training and education demonstrably exert a tremendous influence.... Thus is it certain that education exerteth an influence, and for this reason the Manifestations of God, the Well-Springs of His mercy, are raised up in the world, that through the breaths of holiness They may educate the human race, and make of the suckling child a strong and valiant man.

order.why: Retain the related supplied Tablet excerpt in its own wording.
shortened: No matter how much the shell is educated (or polished), it can never become the radiant pearl. The black stone will not become the world illuming gem. The calocynth and the thorny cactus can never by training and development become the blessed tree. That is to say, training doth not change the human gem (i. e., human nature or entity), but it produceth a marvelous effect. By this effective power all that is registered latent of virtues and capacities in the human reality will be revealed.

order.why: Read the provisional translation’s bird analogy with its authority unchanged.
Keep the supplied account of potentialities in the Bab’s commentary.
Read the Qur’anic verse concerning degrees and ranks.
Consider the Qur’anic speakers’ appointed stations.
Read the later clarification distinguishing inherited and inherent qualities.
Close with the supplied account of a common beginning and differing paths of progress.

questions: How can differences of capacity be acknowledged while equality, dignity, and access to education remain central?
What can an educator reasonably know about someone’s potential, and what should remain open to discovery?
How do the images of gardens, vessels, and a body illuminate different aspects of human diversity?
How does Paul’s account of indispensable and less honored members challenge familiar ways of assigning importance?
What tensions arise between explanations of innate limits and passages about education, effort, and divine grace?
How might a family or community help gifts develop without forcing uniformity or settling into fixed judgments?

references.label: 1 · 1 Corinthians 12:14–26 · The members need one another
references.note: Read Paul’s account of the body in its Christian communal setting: different members belong, apparently weaker members are necessary, and suffering and honor are shared. Compare this account of mutual dependence with the compilation’s eye-and-nail imagery, its affirmation of equality, and its counsel against expecting every perfection in every person.

subjects.displayTitle: Prayers for firmness: strength to serve and unite
subjects.introduction: Make firm my steps and strengthen my back in service to Thy Cause: the prayer for firmness, as ‘Abdu’l-Bahá voices it, is never a request to stand still. It asks for feet that hold on a straight path so that the hands are free to serve, for hearts calmed and breasts expanded, for the scattered gathered and the torn mended until a whole community speaks with a single tongue. Firmness in the Covenant is sought as a gift rather than an achievement, by people who admit that they are helpless, wandering and fallen, and who know that through divine confirmation a feeble ant becomes Solomon. The images give perseverance its vocabulary: rooted trees, mountains at rest, a sheltering cave, gentle breezes and refreshing rain. Many of these supplications arose in seasons of opposition and breach, and their urgency keeps the strain of those years, while others ask for humility, good character, healing and joy, so that steadiness and tenderness grow together. Psalm 51 moves in a kindred way from a renewed spirit toward teaching others. The road continues through firmness in the Covenant, steadfastness under tests, and the daily practice of faithfulness.
subjects.arc: Open with the repair of division and the strength to serve, hear personal and communal petitions for steadiness, attend to their historical struggles, and conclude with renewal, good character, and unity.

order.why: Consider steadfastness through gentle breezes and refreshing showers.
shortened: Grant, O Thou Loving Lord, that all may stand firm and steadfast, shining with everlasting splendour, so that, at every breath, gentle breezes may blow from the bowers of Thy loving-kindness, that from the ocean of Thy grace a mist may rise, that the kindly showers of Thy love may bestow freshness, and the zephyr waft its perfume from the rose garden of divine unity.

order.why: Open with the prayer to gather, mend, and unite.
shortened: O Lord! Unite all that is scattered and unify all that is divided and mend all that is torn, and gather Thy loved ones in assemblies of remembrance and praise, and admit Thy servants into gatherings of light and glory, and make them a single tongue speaking Thy praise and attributes among the concourse of creation, steadfast in Thy covenants among the people, humble, submissive, proclaiming, devoted, and supplicating to Thy Most Glorious Kingdom, beseeching Thy most exalted horizon.

order.why: Connect firm steps immediately with service.
Read calm hearts and expanded understanding alongside a steady path.
shortened: O my God, my Refuge, my Shelter and my Salvation! I beseech the Kingdom of Thy mystery and the Might of Thy Most Holy Being to make our feet firm in Thy manifest Faith and Thy Straight Path, to calm our hearts, illumine our sight, and expand our breasts through the verses of Thy holiness.

order.why: Join firmness with meekness, lowliness, and love kindled in hearts.
Read the Covenant in relation to becoming people of unity.
Consider the prayer for strength through servitude.
shortened: With utmost humility, supplication and entreaty, I beseech His Holiness the Manifest Beauty to make each of His friends a sign of guidance, that they may become detached from all else save Him, become manifestations of sanctification and essences of purification in all perfections in every direction, be pointed to with fingers of praise on the horizon of existence like the shining moon, and supplicate day and night at the Threshold of Oneness that He may strengthen this weak servant through the power of His servitude. This is the utmost of my hope and the ultimate of my purpose and my greatest entreaty to my Lord.

order.why: Hear the simplest communal petition.
shortened: O Lord! Make us steadfast in Thy Covenant and Testament.

order.why: Keep the brief personal request in its own form.
shortened: O Lord! Illumine his brow with the lights of Thy Kingdom, expand his breast with the signs of Thy dominion, and ordain for him every good in the worlds of Thy holiness. Make firm his feet in Thy Covenant and Testament. Verily, Thou art the All-Bountiful.

order.why: Read firmness and an expanded heart together.
shortened: O my God! O my God! Make firm the feet of Thy loved ones in Thy Covenant and Testament, and expand their breasts through the lights of steadfastness in Thy Cause. Verily, Thou art the Mighty, the Powerful.

order.why: Join steady feet with inward light.
shortened: Make firm their feet upon the Covenant and strengthen their hearts through a light shining forth from the Dawning Place of effulgence.

order.why: Consider firmness alongside devotion.
shortened: O Generous One! Grant steadfastness and devotion, and bestow firmness and establishment.

order.why: Read steadfastness as constancy in love.
shortened: Now, O Lord, grant me steadfastness, bestow upon me firmness, that I may remain firm in love for the Dawning-Place of Thy Oneness and derive light from the Sun of Truth.

order.why: Read steadfastness together with the plea for mercy.
shortened: When we are firm and steadfast in Thy Covenant and Faith, we shun all else but Thee. O Lord! Have mercy and grant steadfastness.

order.why: Hear the request for preservation through severe tests.
Keep Covenant, Cause, and love together.
Join holding fast with praise.
Read the petition for the servants’ shared path.
Let the prayer’s horizon extend to all.
Consider mountains as an image of tranquility as well as firmness.
shortened: O Lord! Aid Thy loved ones to remain firm upon Thy path whereon feet have slipped. Make their hearts steadfast in Thy love and make them as immovable mountains in constancy, firmness and tranquility.

order.why: Read assurance as strength renewed moment by moment.
shortened: Convey greetings to the handmaiden of God, the assured leaf, and the mother of Mashhadi 'Ali. We beseech divine grace that He may grant them new strength of assurance at every moment.

order.why: Hear the concise appeal for firmness in love and the Cause.
shortened: I beseech Thee to make me steadfast in Thy love and firm in Thy Cause. Verily Thou art the Almighty over what Thou willest.

order.why: Keep the threefold petition for Cause, religion, and love.
shortened: Praise be unto Thee for having guided me unto Thy path and caused me to hear Thy call. I beseech Thee to make me steadfast in Thy Cause, firm in Thy religion, and immovable in Thy love.

order.why: Read the stars and suns of utterance as the prayer’s setting.
shortened: O Lord! I beseech Thee by the stars of the heaven of Thy utterance and the suns of Thy favors to aid me to remain firm in the Most Great Steadfastness.

order.why: Consider the invocation of dawn and winds.
shortened: I beseech Thee, O Cleaver of the Dawn and Sender of the Winds, by Thy Most Great Name through which the peoples are impelled, to strengthen whomsoever hath turned towards Thee upon the Most Great Steadfastness.

order.why: Keep the invocation of manifestation and calling.
shortened: I beseech Thee by Thy Manifestation, Thy rising up, and Thy call, to make me one of them who have stood firm in this Cause, mighty and great.

order.why: Read the seat of truth in relation to firmness.
shortened: Say: O my Lord! Establish for me a seat of truth with Thee, then make me firm in this mighty Cause.

order.why: Hear the prayer for another person’s steadiness and well-being.
shortened: Then assist him, O my God, with Thy help, and grant him that which is best for him from the Kingdom of the dominion of the heavens and earth, and make him steadfast in Thy love, and establish him upon Thy path, lest his feet slip from Thy straight way.

order.why: Join strength, assistance, and protection.
shortened: O my God, strengthen my feet in Thy Cause, then make me a helper of Thy Beauty, the Ancient and Resplendent One. Then preserve me within the shelter of Thy protection, and grant me that which Thou hast ordained for Thy sincere servants.

order.why: Consider the recognition that even mystics may lose their footing.
Read the appeal to hold fast amid powers of heaven and earth.
shortened: I beseech Thee, O my Lord, by the Tablet which Thou hast adorned with the lights of Thy utterance and wherein Thou hast written for Thy loved ones that which behooveth them in Thy days, and by Thy Name, the Manifest, the Speaking, the Hidden, and by Thy Light, the Shining, the Radiant, the Treasured, to assist me to hold fast unto Thy Most Great Handle in such wise that neither the hosts of Thy earth and heaven nor the might of the oppressors among Thy creatures shall keep me back from Thee.

order.why: Keep detachment and the cord together.
Connect steadfastness with drawing near to grace.
Read the Tree’s branches nourished by bounty and mercy.
shortened: I beseech Thee by the waves of the sea of Thy oneness, and by the establishment of the throne of Thy grandeur, and by the remembrances of the leaves of the Tree of Thy singleness, to rain down from the heaven of Thy bounty upon the branches of this Tree that which will make them steadfast in Thy love and cause them to drink at all times the wine of Thy mercy.

order.why: Consider growth and freshness alongside remaining firm.
Read the gathered birds and the winds of tests.
shortened: My God, my God! By how You have gathered these birds in the garden of Your sanctification and the meadows of Your oneness, make their feet firm upon Your path and make them steadfast in Your ancient Covenant and Testament, O Lord of the Worlds, that they may not be shaken by the winds of tests and trials.

order.why: Read signs and standards of steadfastness in the prayer’s full available wording.
shortened: O my God, my God! Make firm the steps of Thy loved ones in Thy straight path, Thine ancient Covenant and Thy firm and excellent Testament.

O Lord! Make them signs of firmness and standards of steadfastness in the realm of existence, holding fast to the sure handle, O my Most Exalted Lord, and clinging to the firm cord, O God of the heavens and earths.

order.why: Keep the mountain and pillar images in their prayerful setting.
shortened: O Lord! Make firm their feet in Thy religion and guard their hearts from the doubts of those heedless of Thy remembrance and make them mountains firm in Thy Covenant and pillars fixed in Thy Testament.

order.why: Read the garden of the heart and the clouds of harmony.
Join remembrance, a quickened spirit, and strengthened service.
shortened: O Lord! Make his feet firm in Thy Covenant and Testament, perfume his nostrils with Thy fragrances, quicken his spirit with Thy breezes, expand his breast through Thy remembrance, and strengthen his back with the hosts of Thy confirmation and assistance.

order.why: Consider sincerity and gladness beside firm steps.
shortened: O Lord! Make firm his steps in Thy Cause, expand his breast through Thy light, gladden his spirit through Thy victories, spread through him Thy remembrance, cause him to speak forth Thy praise, attire him in the robe of sincerity in Thy Cause, and admit him into the garden of immortality through Thy grace.

order.why: Read faith, assurance, mercy, and love together.
shortened: I beseech God to increase thy faith and certitude, to strengthen thy steadfastness and firmness, to immerse thee in the seas of His mercy, to guide thee to the kingdom of His grace and bounty, to make thee a sign of His love and a word of the Manifestation of His Will, and to illumine thy face among the believers.

order.why: Hear the prayer for intimacy with mysteries and companionship in remembrance.
Keep the prayer for the hearts of the handmaidens.
shortened: O Lord! Make firm the hearts of Thy sanctified handmaidens in Thy Covenant and Testament.

order.why: Read the intercession for a woman, her children, and descendants.
shortened: Make this assured handmaiden of Yours, along with her children and descendants, firm and steadfast in Your Covenant and Testament. Make her strong and unwavering in Your Pact.

order.why: Consider the family’s continuing life within the prayer’s wider horizon.
Read the recollection of childhood nurture and the endurance of hardship.
Keep the long history of service and renewed guidance in this personal prayer.
Read Samandar’s trials through the imagery of fire and refined gold.
Hear the joy at Faran’s preservation through tests.
Read a blessing on the loved ones and a particular supplicant.
Consider the brothers’ service, recognition, and need for assistance.
shortened: O Lord! Aid these brothers to serve the Covenant and to be illumined by the lights of the emanations of the Kingdom throughout all regions, to drink from the cup of Thy favors which overflows with the wine of recognition among the people of constancy. Assist them through Thy Word, bestow upon them Thy bounty, shower upon them Thy mercy, and help them in all things.

order.why: Read the maidservant’s service to those who remain firm.
Hear the petition for a woman’s praise and steadfast service.
shortened: I beseech Thee, O Cleaver of Dawn and Subjugator of Winds, by Thy Name through which Thou hast subdued all names, to make this leaf of Thine confirmed by Thy confirmations, uttering Thy praise among Thy handmaidens, and steadfast in Thy service.

order.why: Keep the prayer for the Afnan and the acts that win divine approval.
shortened: Glory be unto Thee, O my God! I beseech Thee by the fragrances of the hearts of them that know Thee and by the burning of the livers of the sincere ones in their separation and remoteness from Thee, to assist Thy Afnan in that which Thou lovest and approvest. Then raise them at all times through Thy grace, Thy power and Thy loving-kindness.

order.why: Read the reported prayer for assistance from the Supreme Concourse.
Keep the chosen ones’ prayer for strength with its source omission visible.
